You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel — Buyer's Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**Privileged & confidential — prepared for Wattlebridge Holdings deal team**

Before the substance, a framing point. The Seller's preamble asserts these terms are "FINAL," "settled at principal level," and "not intended to be re-opened," and recites a "market context" paragraph. Treat this as negotiating anchor, not fact. Several of the "standard market" claims are simply wrong for a deal of this type (I flag them below), and nothing stops us marking up a draft. Please confirm with your principals whether any of these were in fact conceded at principal level — my working assumption is that they were not, and the Disclosure Letter itself contradicts several of the Seller's "it's handled" assertions.

The two most damaging structural issues are the **combination of (a) general disclosure of the entire data room and (b) a deemed/constructive buyer-knowledge bar**. Together these largely gut the warranty package. I deal with those first.

---

## A. Structural issues that hollow out the warranties

### 1. Deemed buyer knowledge — Clause 8.3 (push back hard)
The Seller wants no claim for any matter the Buyer "or its advisers had knowledge" of, "including any matter **discoverable** from the data room or public records." This is *constructive* knowledge, not actual knowledge. It means anything we could theoretically have found defeats a claim. The Seller's claim that this is "standard" is incorrect — a deemed-discoverability bar is aggressive and not market.

**Position:** Limit to the *actual* knowledge of a short list of named deal-team individuals, as at signing. Delete "discoverable," "advisers," and "public records." A warranty we can't rely on because we "should have found" the problem is worthless.

### 2. General/sweeping disclosure — Disclosure Letter 1.1, 1.2 (push back hard)
Clause 1.1 purports to disclose "**every fact, matter and circumstance** contained or referred to" in the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), plus the Accounts and public registers. Clause 1.4 then says nothing in the letter admits anything. So the Seller discloses the whole room against all warranties but admits nothing — the mirror image of issue 1. Anything buried in the data room becomes "disclosed," so no claim.

**Position:** Reject general/data-room-wide disclosure. Require **specific disclosure only**, disclosed against identified warranties, and a "**fairly disclosed**" standard (disclosed with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter and allow a reasonable buyer to assess it). Public registers should not be a disclosure source.

### 3. Exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" — 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (push back)
Applying non-reliance, exclusive-remedy and the limitations to *all* claims will, on its face, capture fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation.

**Position:** A universal **fraud carve-out** from every limitation, cap, time bar, disclosure and knowledge qualification (fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment/default). This is non-negotiable and genuinely standard.

---

## B. Caps, baskets and time limits

### 4. Fundamental / title warranties capped and time-limited as general — "administrative simplicity" (push back hard)
This is the most objectionable "market" claim. Capacity and **title** warranties should be **uncapped (or capped at 100% of price)** and survive for a long/indefinite period. If title to the shares fails, we could lose the entire company yet recover only AUD 4.8m. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept catastrophic downside.

**Position:** Fundamental/title warranties — cap = 100% of price (AUD 24m); limitation period 7 years (or indefinite for title).

### 5. General cap — Clause 12.1 (negotiate)
20% / AUD 4.8m sits within a defensible range but at the Seller-friendly end only after we also fix issues 1–4; otherwise the cap is academic. Push toward a higher cap and, more importantly, ring-fence the specific-indemnity items below so they sit **outside** the general cap.

### 6. Basket / de minimis — Clause 12.2 (negotiate)
De minimis AUD 25k and basket AUD 250k (~1% of price) are roughly market. But the Seller proposes an **excess-only** basket (deductible — recover only above AUD 250k).

**Position:** Seek a **tipping/first-dollar basket** (once AUD 250k is reached, recover from dollar one). At minimum, trade this against the cap.

### 7. Time limits — Clause 12.3 / 13 (push back)
18 months for general warranties is acceptable. But "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all** Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" sweeps **tax** and **fundamental** warranties into 18 months. That is not market.

**Position:** Tax warranties and the tax covenant/indemnity survive to the **statutory limitation period** (c. 7 years); fundamental/title as per issue 4. General and business warranties 18 months is fine.

---

## C. Debt, leakage and funds flow (debt-free/cash-free baseline)

### 8. Riverlark facility ~AUD 3.2m — Clause 2 / 7 (push back hard)
The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility is **not repaid and security not discharged**, yet the Seller proposes a release "following Completion." Under a debt-free/cash-free deal we will not take the company with undischarged security on a promise.

**Position:** Repayment in full **at Completion** out of the proceeds via the funds flow, with an **executed discharge/release of security delivered at Completion** (and payout letter pre-Completion). The AUD 3.2m reduces the equity proceeds — confirm it is reflected in the funds flow.

### 9. DD-005 Completion bonuses AUD 420k — Funds flow (push back)
The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller" and deliberately omits them from the funds flow. But they are **triggered by Completion** — classic change-of-control/transaction leakage that the *company* will likely bear post-Completion. The disclosure also leaves **payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs** open.

**Position:** Treat the bonuses **plus all on-costs (super, payroll tax)** as a Seller liability — either paid by Seller pre-Completion or deducted in the funds flow as a debt-like/leakage item. Get a specific indemnity for any shortfall and gross-up for on-costs.

### 10. Sandbar supplier renewals AUD 330k — DD-008 / DD-011 (investigate)
Three "related" renewals of exactly AUD 110k each. The disclosure flags they should be "read together" and does **not** confirm they are ordinary-course, terminable or unavoidable. The identical sizing invites the question of whether they were split to sit under an individual consent/materiality threshold.

**Position:** Obtain the contracts; confirm term, termination rights, accrual and whether committed around Completion. If new committed spend, treat as leakage or require it as a pre-Completion conduct/consent item.

---

## D. Business-critical specific risks (need specific indemnities / conditions)

### 11. Bluefen change-of-control — Clause 3 / 6.3 (push back hard)
Bluefen is **~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue** and has a change-control consent requirement (cl 11.2, conditions 11.3). The Disclosure Letter confirms there is **no final written consent and the conditions are not satisfied**. Yet the Seller offers only "reasonable endeavours" and deems consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" — ignoring the 11.3 conditions.

**Position:** Make obtaining the Bluefen consent (consent **and** satisfaction of the 11.3 conditions) a **Condition Precedent to Completion**, upgrade to "best endeavours," and if it can't be a CP, price-protect it (retention/earn-out adjustment and/or specific uncapped indemnity for loss of Bluefen). Losing 30% of revenue post-Completion would materially re-set the valuation.

### 12. Ironquay IP — Clause 11.1 / DL 4 (push back)
Under DD-004 cl 7.3, SOW3 **Project Materials (IP) only transfer on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee**; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open, with no proof of payment or confirmatory assignment. The real risk isn't the AUD 180k fee — it's that **the company may not own SOW3 IP** at all. The Seller's indemnity, limited to the SOW3 payment, does not cover loss of the IP. For a SaaS target, IP ownership is the core asset.

**Position:** Pre-Completion, obtain proof of payment **and** a confirmatory IP assignment; a specific IP-ownership warranty; and a specific indemnity covering loss/impairment of the SOW3 IP (not just the fee), outside the general cap.

### 13. Export/privacy incident DD-006 — Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (push back hard)
A download link to ~1,240 personal records (names, business emails, roles, activity) sent to an unintended external address. The Seller characterises it as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Under the Privacy Act / Notifiable Data Breaches scheme this can trigger **assessment and OAIC/individual notification obligations** and regulatory/remediation exposure; the disclosure itself concedes scope, access and notification are unresolved.

**Position:** Do **not** accept the "not material" characterisation. Require (i) completion of the investigation and a status report pre-Completion, (ii) a data-protection compliance warranty, and (iii) a **specific indemnity for the incident** (regulatory fines, notification/remediation, third-party claims) sitting **outside** the basket and cap.

### 14. Title evidence — DD-012 (verify)
Title is evidenced only by the share register, and the Seller notes we have not done our own verification.

**Position:** Current ASIC/PPSR searches; confirm no encumbrances over the shares; a strong, uncapped title warranty (per issue 4).

### 15. Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009) — (verify, lower priority)
A share sale usually doesn't trigger assignment/consent, but both contracts should be checked for **change-of-control** notice/consent/termination triggers (the lease has a notification obligation; Mossvale restricts assignment). Low risk but confirm, and comply with any notice obligation.

---

## E. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

**Reject outright / non-negotiable:**
1. Fraud carve-out from all limitations, disclosure and knowledge qualifications.
2. Delete constructive/deemed buyer knowledge (8.3) — actual knowledge of named individuals only; delete "discoverable"/public records/advisers.
3. Reject whole-data-room general disclosure — specific disclosure only, "fairly disclosed" standard.
4. Fundamental/title warranties uncapped (or 100% of price) with long/indefinite survival; tax to statutory period.

**Deal-protection must-haves:**
5. Bluefen consent + 11.3 conditions as a Condition Precedent (best endeavours); fallback specific indemnity/price protection — ~30% of revenue at stake.
6. Riverlark AUD 3.2m repaid and security discharged **at** Completion, reflected in funds flow.
7. Specific indemnities outside the cap/basket for: the privacy incident (DD-006), Ironquay SOW3 IP ownership (not just the fee), and the DD-005 bonuses plus on-costs.
8. DD-005 bonuses + super/payroll tax treated as Seller liability/leakage in the funds flow.

**Negotiate / trade:**
9. General cap — push above 20% and keep specific indemnities outside it.
10. Tipping basket rather than excess-only; de minimis/basket otherwise acceptable.
11. Separate tax covenant and IP warranty suite (core SaaS asset).

**Verify in diligence:**
12. Sandbar renewals (ordinary-course / terminable / split-to-avoid-threshold question), lease and Mossvale change-of-control triggers, title/PPSR searches.

**Correct the record with the Seller:** the preamble's "market" claims on fundamental-warranty caps, tax survival and buyer knowledge are not standard; I'd reply that we do not accept the "FINAL / not to be re-opened" framing and are marking up accordingly.

If helpful, I can turn this into a markup/issues list against the clause numbers or draft the specific-indemnity and CP language for items 5–8. Want me to prepare that next?

Note: I've reviewed only the Seller's summary and Disclosure Letter — I have not seen the underlying DD-002–DD-012 documents or the operative SPA clauses themselves, so some positions should be confirmed against the full drafts.
=== END ADVICE ===
